title: Freddie Mac CRT Disclosure Analytics
summary: A live collateral-surveillance workbench that connects portfolio delinquency movement to the complete masked Freddie Mac CRT loan-period disclosure record.
outcome: Delivered bounded public investigation across 20,439,666 masked loan-period rows, exact portfolio rate-and-mix attribution, private object storage, authenticated data retrieval, and a zero-incremental-cost production release.

deployment.provider: Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, and Cloudflare R2
deployment.runtime: Static review docket with a bounded Python query function and authenticated GET-only object gateway

architecture: The private build plane streams the approved Clarity archive into 292 source-faithful Parquet partitions and calculates versioned surveillance measures in DuckDB.
A release builder preserves all accepted rows, adds three lineage columns, and replaces the original loan identifier and ZIP3 with stable keyed tokens before publication.
The 292 immutable masked Parquet assets live in a private Cloudflare R2 bucket with no public bucket endpoint.
A Cloudflare Worker accepts only authenticated GET requests for one exact allowlisted object under the fixed release prefix.
A Vercel Python function validates deal, period, status, limit, and offset, fetches one partition with a server-side token, and returns no more than 50 rows.
The browser renders the risk-committee review docket and record register without receiving storage URLs, service credentials, raw identifiers, or restricted build artifacts.
evaluation: A complete scan reconciled 20,439,666 release rows to 20,439,666 foundation rows and 292 public assets to 292 deal-month groups.
Every public row passed the required loan-token and ZIP3-token formats while retaining all 96 stored columns.
Aggregate measures reconcile exactly across 292 shared groups, and portfolio D60+ movement decomposes exactly into deal rate and exposure-mix contributions.

Hosted verification covered private-bucket configuration, anonymous denial, authenticated object parity, Vercel API responses, pagination, 96-field detail, security headers, browser runtime, and rollback retention.
Desktop and mobile Chromium checks found zero automated WCAG A/AA violations and no application errors.
operationalTradeoffs: Private R2 separates data retention from Git publication and offers more free-tier headroom than Vercel Blob, but adds one Worker and one shared service token.
Deal-month Parquet retrieval keeps the serving path simple and bounded, but broad cross-partition queries remain a local analytical workflow.
The public API caps page size at 50 rows and offset at 150,000, favoring investigation over bulk download.
Workers Free provides a hard 100,000-request daily ceiling and keeps incremental cost at $0, but it is not an availability commitment.
R2 SQL or a hosted analytical database remains deferred until measured latency, concurrency, growth, or query-shape evidence justifies it.
disclaimer: This portfolio product uses Freddie Mac public disclosure data with selected fields masked before serving. It supports descriptive collateral-surveillance investigation only and must not be used for borrower decisions, re-identification, outside-data matching, forecasts, causal claims, or investment recommendations.

story.recruiterSummary: This product answers a capital-markets review question: which CRT exposures deteriorated, how much did each deal contribute, and what disclosed records support the investigation? It preserves the complete approved archive, makes rate-versus-mix attribution explicit, and serves masked records through a private-storage boundary with measured evidence and honest decision limits.
story.technicalNarrative: The private build plane validates historical 89, 90, and 93-field layouts, writes 292 source-faithful Parquet partitions, and calculates metric version m8.1.0 in DuckDB. The public release builder retains every accepted row, adds lineage, and replaces loan identifier and ZIP3 with stable keyed tokens. Immutable masked assets move to private R2. An authenticated GET-only Worker exposes one exact object to a Vercel Python function, which validates bounded filters and returns at most 50 records. The static browser surface combines a filed-sheet risk review with masked record pagination and 96-field detail. Source data, storage, serving, and browser lifecycles remain separate.
scalabilityRoadmap: Measure production latency, cache hit rate, and concurrent browsing before changing the deal-month object design.
Introduce R2 SQL or a hosted analytical database only when cross-partition query demand or measured concurrency exceeds the current bounded function.
Automate immutable monthly release promotion and token rotation after a real new-month archive has exercised the documented runbook.
Add Firefox, Safari, assistive-technology, and field-performance evidence before making broader experience claims.
story.executiveSummary: The live workbench connects portfolio-level D60+ movement to full masked Freddie Mac CRT disclosure records. It covers 20.4 million loan-period rows, distinguishes deal deterioration from portfolio contribution, and keeps complete Parquet objects behind authenticated server-to-server access. The release costs $0 incrementally and carries a hard free-plan request ceiling, but remains a descriptive portfolio demonstration rather than an operational investment or borrower-decision system.
story.intendedUser: A capital-markets credit analyst, collateral-surveillance reviewer, data engineering reviewer, or hiring manager assessing analytical controls and public-cloud delivery.

Open the corresponding masked deal-month register and page through complete disclosure rows

technologyDecisions.rationale: The measured 20.4 million-row workload meets refresh and query budgets locally while preserving exact source grain and one-file pruning.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Provision a cloud warehouse before measuring need
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The design is single-user and batch-oriented, but avoids paid infrastructure and extra governance until scale evidence requires it.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Cross-period investigation needs a persistent pseudonymous loan key without publishing the original loan identifier or ZIP3.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Publish original identifiers or aggregate away every record
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Stable tokens preserve analytical linkage but do not remove the linkage risk of all other disclosed field combinations.

technologyDecisions.technology: Private R2 with an authenticated Worker
technologyDecisions.rationale: Object storage separates data lifecycle from Git, retains free-tier headroom, and keeps bucket locations and credentials out of the browser.
technologyDecisions.alternative: GitHub release assets, public R2, or Vercel Blob
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The narrow gateway adds one service and one rotating secret, while avoiding public bulk objects and a nearly exhausted storage allowance.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Server-side validation and paging support record investigation without shipping service credentials or exposing unrestricted object access.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Direct browser access or a persistent analytical API
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Queries are limited to one deal-month partition and 50 rows per response, which favors review over bulk exploration.

limitations: Stable masking removes the original loan identifier and ZIP3, but other public disclosure fields may remain linkable to the source release.

The public API is intentionally bounded and does not support bulk or arbitrary cross-partition queries.

bulletCandidates.bullet: Built a Freddie Mac CRT surveillance product across 20.4 million loan-period records, reconciling 292 deal-month groups exactly and decomposing portfolio D60+ change into signed deal rate and exposure-mix contributions.

Designed a source-faithful DuckDB and Parquet pipeline with historical schema controls, stable keyed masking, one-file partition pruning, append-only refresh, failure recovery, and 0.588 ms materialized-query p95.

Delivered a zero-incremental-cost public workbench backed by 292 private R2 assets, an authenticated GET-only Cloudflare Worker, and a bounded Vercel API that exposes complete masked records without shipping storage credentials to the browser.
